title: Introduce telemetry debouncing layer and token snapshot collector
author: Leah Martinez
description:
Background: High-frequency token-level counters and span churn were causing both metric cardinality spikes and a large volume of small traces during bursty traffic patterns. This created noisy alerting and increased backend storage costs without improving signal for SRE and product analysts.

Motivation: Add a lightweight debouncing layer that groups rapid consecutive emissions for the same invocation path into a single summarized telemetry sample, plus a token snapshot collector that captures a compact per-invocation token histogram and KV-cache snapshot for post-hoc analysis. Goals: reduce cardinality and storage for high-volume paths, preserve tail signal for troubleshooting, and expose knobs for staged rollout.

What this PR does (high level): Implements a telemetry debouncing middleware in the serving runtime and a small collector that emits a compact token-snapshot protobuf to the tracing/telemetry pipeline. The debounce layer collapses emissions within a configurable window (default 150ms) per route + model-version key and emits an aggregated sample with counters, min/max/median token latency buckets, and a sha256 token-shape fingerprint. The token snapshot collector captures a 64-bin token-length histogram, KV-cache hit ratio, and a lightweight context anchor (stable sampling id). Both components are feature-flagged and opt-in by config (telemetry.debounce.enabled=false by default).

Compatibility and migration: Default behavior is unchanged. Config flags exist at process and tenant level for early enablement. When enabled, dashboards and alerts have a compatibility mapping layer that allows SRE to compare pre- and post-debounce metrics for two weeks before switching primary alerts. A migration playbook is included in docs/observability/migrations/telemetry-debounce.md.

Implementation details: - Debounce middleware implemented in runtime/telemetry/debounce.go, with an in-memory LRU keyed by route:model:request-shape and a single-threaded coalescer for emission. - Snapshot collector implemented as runtime/telemetry/snapshot_collector.go; snapshots are serialized using the existing compact-proto format and sent to the telemetry ingestion topic with a new msg-type header (snap-v1). - Added a metrics shim that exposes both raw and debounced counters under telemetry.raw.* and telemetry.debounced.* so dashboards can overlay them. - Added an agent-side config (agent/config/telemetry.yaml) and an operator toggle (console feature flag) for rollout.

Files changed: See files_changed for a curated list (small diffs). No protocol-breaking changes to existing trace schema; new snapshot schema is backwards compatible and ignored by older consumers.

Testing: Unit tests cover debounce bucketing logic and collector serialization. Integration tests added that run a traffic replay (tools/replay) with bursty input to assert >65% reduction in emitted metric samples for synthetic hot paths while retaining >98th percentile latency fidelity within 5% margin. Load test in perf-canary shows 30% lower ingestion QPS for telemetry at 95th percentile production paths.

Rollout plan: 1) Enable feature flag for internal staging and perf-canary for 48 hours. 2) Enable for 10% tenants with telemetry monitoring dashboards comparing raw vs debounced. 3) Ramp to 50% over 48 hours if no alert regressions. 4) Flip to default-on after two weeks and update alerting to use debounced signals.

Checklist: - [x] debounce implementation and unit tests - [x] snapshot collector and serialization - [x] dashboards and example queries (docs/dashboards/debounce) - [x] migration playbook - [x] perf canary run and results summary attached - [x] CI green

Related work: Supplements previous token-level sampling and rollup PRs by providing a low-overhead consolidation mechanism; complements the session-reassembler work by reducing emission noise at the source. Linked Linear items and a support ticket are referenced below.

release_notes: Add telemetry debouncing middleware and token snapshot collector. Feature-flagged; opt-in via telemetry.debounce.enabled. New dashboards and migration playbook included. Reduces telemetry emission volume for bursty paths while preserving tail signal for troubleshooting.
notes_for_sre: Dashboards added under Observability -> Debounce. Keep telemetry.raw.* on the left axis and telemetry.debounced.* on the right for the first two weeks. Alerts have been duplicated with a prefixed 'debounced/' and set to monitor both signals during rollout. Watch for mismatches where debounced signal diverges >10% on 99th percentile.
perf_results_summary: Perf canary on 2025-01-10: synthetic burst replay showed median ingestion QPS reduction of 28% and 95th percentile ingestion QPS reduction of 30% for targeted hot routes. Token-latency 98th percentile remained within 4% of baseline across runs. Detailed artifacts in perf/perf-canary/debounce_run_2025-01-10.yaml
security_review: no-secret-paths-introduced; snapshot payloads are hashed and do not include plaintext customer prompts. Security approved.
